title: Kyo: a book-style guide to the documentation
byline: Kyo maintainers (Flavio Brasil and contributors) · getkyo.io, documentation for v1.0.0-RC7 (September 2026), Apache 2.0
note: Kyo has no book; its documentation is the set of per-module READMEs published at getkyo.io. This page arranges that documentation like a book, in a suggested reading order: the introduction, the core modules, writing styles, concurrency, testing, then applications. Every section links straight to its heading on getkyo.io (the latest release). Terms under each section are its sub-headings in the docs. Summaries are in our own words.
summary: Kyo is a Scala 3 toolkit built on algebraic effects. A computation has type A < S: it produces an A once every effect in the row S has been handled, and S is an intersection type, so effects combine in any order and each handler removes one. Pure effects (Abort, Env, Var, Choice, Emit, Stream) live in kyo-prelude; kyo-core adds Sync, Async, fibers, Scope and concurrency primitives; kyo-kernel exposes the machinery (ArrowEffect, ContextEffect, handlers with continuations) for writing new effects. Around that core sit direct-style and combinator dialects, STM and actors, a work-stealing scheduler, a test framework, derived schemas, HTTP, typed LLM programs (kyo-ai) and bridges to ZIO and other runtimes.
